summary: Implemented generated file-based Kanban, task cards and machine view with atomic claim-next, owner progress/heartbeat, block/resume/release, priority and path reservations. make check passes 42 tests; 99 local Markdown links and all 20 cards were reviewed. Concurrent and partial-publication failure cases pass.
limitations: Owner labels and heartbeats are cooperative reports, not authentication or process liveness detection. Stale claims are never reassigned automatically.
fcntl coordinates one shared local filesystem ledger; it does not coordinate independent machines or copied worktree ledgers.
Path reservations enforce CLI claims, not arbitrary filesystem edits. Broad pending boundaries intentionally serialize overlapping work.
Multi-file publication is not one filesystem transaction. Canonical state commits first; the checksum index is written last, and repair is explicit after a publication error.
This does not spawn agents or run calendar jobs; parallel implementation still requires explicit authorization and separate worktrees.
Host-only work: no phone commands, APK installation or native actions. Historical evidence, existing task/experiment records and scope permissions were preserved.
